questions.question: How should the key parameter treat `.` and `..` segments?

options.label: B: no navigation (Recommended)
options.description: `.`/`..` stay ordinary names, matching spec 051 and research §6 as written. Accepting a key means parse it or reject it; callers resolve relative paths themselves. Smallest surface and nothing becomes unreachable.

options.label: A: reserve at the API
options.description: The library rejects any key with a `.` or `..` segment, and navigation steps reduce against a base key. Spec 051 isn't amended (its Layering paragraph allows a subset), but entities named `.`/`..` can't be reached through the library.

options.label: Defer until spec 004 is read
options.description: RemotePath may already decide this. Settle it after checking spec 004 rather than choosing in the abstract.

questions.question: When `..` would climb above the base (e.g. `../x` at the root), what happens?

options.label: Reject (Recommended)
options.description: The path is refused with an error. Climbing out of a child store's scope fails loudly instead of silently landing somewhere else.

options.label: Clamp at the root
options.description: Stop at the root the way POSIX does with `/..` and URL resolution does: `../x` at the root means `x`. Never fails, but a mistaken path can quietly address the wrong entity.

questions.question: How are separator variants handled: `a//b`, a trailing `a/`, a leading `/a`?

options.label: Collapse all three (Recommended)
options.description: Treat them as path noise, like navigation: `a//b` becomes `a/b`, `a/` becomes `a`, `/a` becomes `a`. Matches what users expect from paths; several spellings map to one Key on input, while Keys stay unique.

options.label: Reject all three
options.description: Only `.` and `..` count as navigation; anything else that isn't Key-shaped is an error. Stricter, and one spelling per Key on input too.

options.label: Collapse some
options.description: For example, allow a leading `/` and a trailing `/` but reject `//`. Say which in the notes.

questions.question: What can a `..` climb to?

options.label: The store's own root (Recommended)
options.description: Drop the general base: every walk starts at the root of the store being called (a child store's root for a child). `..` past that root is rejected. This removes the 4.1/4.3 contradiction; the child-store details stay [check 015].

options.label: Keep a general base b
options.description: Keep a base inside a store as a concept (for a future working-folder or relative-key API). Then decide whether `..` may climb above b up to the root, or escapes at b.

questions.question: When are the backend's string rules (§3a) checked during reduction?

options.label: On the end position only (Recommended)
options.description: Walk first, then check the resulting Key as a whole: segment rules and total length. `CON/../a` is accepted as `a`. Reduction then decides equivalence exactly, and the length gap closes.

options.label: Every down step and the end
options.description: A name that is popped again must still pass (`CON/../a` rejected). Then the equivalence in 4.2 has to also require every step to pass, so it is no longer defined by end position alone.

questions.question: `..` mid-path: concept reduces `a/c/../b` to `a/b`, spec 004 (PATH-003) rejects every `..`. Which wins?

options.label: Keep PATH-003, rejected (Recommended)
options.description: Rewrite concept §4 so partial navigation means `.` and separators only; `..` is reserved and rejected. No behavior change, no breaking change; the escape rule becomes a special case.

options.label: Relax PATH-003
options.description: Keep concept §4 as it is; spec 004 changes so `..` climbs within the root. Inputs that raise InvalidPath today start succeeding; PATH-003's tests and example change; needs a backlog item.

questions.question: Backslash: spec 004 rewrites `\` to `/` (PATH-002). How does the concept treat it?

options.label: Adopt PATH-002 (Recommended)
options.description: `\` is a separator in the input, so `a\b` is equivalent to `a/b`; names containing `\` are unreachable, like `..`. §3a drops `\` from the name filters and §4.1 lists it as a separator.

options.label: Flag PATH-002 as a delta
options.description: The concept keeps `\` as a name character that backends filter; record PATH-002 as a conflict to resolve later (it costs S3 keys that contain `\`).

questions.question: How the root is written: spec 004 uses `.` (str, name, parts), and a single-component path has parent None; spec 051 has ROOT name ε and parent of `a` is the root. What does the concept record?

options.label: Record as open delta (Recommended)
options.description: Concept states the model view (ε, parent = root) and lists rows 10-12 as conflicts with spec 004 for a backlog item. Nothing in 004 changes now; any change there is breaking and its own decision.

options.label: Treat `.` as presentation only
options.description: Concept explicitly says `str(ROOT) == "."` is a display spelling in the root's class, not its Key, and accepts parent None as API convenience. Closes the question without a backlog item; rows 11 (name, parts) stay in tension with TREE-007.

questions.question: Which of these points should go into the concept now?

options.label: Rule floor (#1, #2)
options.description: A library-wide acceptance floor below the tiers (null byte; segments exactly `.`/`..`), with names like `a..b` and `.hidden` stated as ordinary.

options.label: Key as a value type (#3, #4, #5)
options.description: The key type is built only by reduction, immutable, compares and hashes by canonical form (realizing ≈), and is not a local path.

options.label: Key operations (#6, #7)
options.description: Segments, name, parent and join defined on Keys, with join as walk continuation; the root case marked open.

options.label: Round trip + root per operation (#8)
options.description: Printed keys reduce back to themselves; accepting the root key is a per-operation predicate.

questions.question: Open item 1: which spec owns the equivalence ≈ (and with it ν, L_floor and the tiers)?

options.label: New key spec (Recommended)
options.description: This concept becomes its own spec, between 051 (tree) and 004 (RemotePath). It owns key strings, ν, ≈, the tiers and resolution. 051 stays untouched; 004 becomes one realization of ν and links to it.

options.label: Amend spec 004
options.description: ν and ≈ become PATH clauses. One fewer spec, but 004 is about RemotePath, a code value object, so model content and API surface get mixed; resolution (§5) has no natural home there.

options.label: Extend spec 051
options.description: Add them as TREE sections. Conflicts with 051's own scope: 'structure only, at one instant: no operation, backend or encoding'. ν reads input and the tiers are backend constraints, so 051's overview would have to change.

questions.question: Open item 2a: backslash. Spec 004 (PATH-002) rewrites `\` to `/`; the concept treats `\` as a name character a backend may refuse. Which does the model take?

options.label: Separator in the input (Recommended)
options.description: In R, `\` is read like `/`: `a\b` ≈ `a/b`. Users on Windows get the path they expect; names containing `\` become unreachable, which joins L_floor (no segment contains `\`). Spec 004 already does this.

options.label: Name character
options.description: `\` reaches the name, and only backends that refuse it (L_b) reject it. S3 keys with `\` stay reachable; `a\b` on Windows is one name, not two; PATH-002 becomes a delta to change in 004.

questions.question: Open item 2b: the root's display spelling. Spec 051 fixes the root's key string as ε; spec 004 prints it as `.`. What does the model say?

options.label: Key is ε; display is out of scope (Recommended)
options.description: The model only fixes ε and notes that `.` round-trips (ν(`.`) = ε). How a value prints is a realization choice for 004; nothing more to decide at model level.

options.label: Mandate ε for display too
options.description: The model requires the root to be shown as its key string ε. Spec 004's `.` (str, name, parts) becomes a delta to fix, which is a breaking change there.

questions.question: Accept that `\` can never be part of a name, so objects with `\` in their name (legal on S3/Azure) are unreachable in every mode?

options.label: Accept (Recommended)
options.description: Exactly your proposal: convert or reject, never a name. `\` joins the floor; the cost is recorded in the concept like the `.`/`..` cost.

options.label: Add a third mode: literal
options.description: Non-native backends may also choose Sep_S = {`/`} with `\` kept as a name character, so such objects stay reachable. Three modes instead of two; `a\b` means different things per store.

questions.question: BlockedByItem in a write (`write("f/x")` where `f` is an item): which spec-005 error?

options.label: InvalidPath (Recommended)
options.description: Extend ERR-005 (b) from 'the path names the wrong node type' to 'the path or one of its prefixes does'. The key is well formed, an entity on its way has the wrong kind; this is the same failure one level up.

options.label: NotFound
options.description: Treat it as 'the parent folder does not exist', which is true in the model (no folder f). Simpler, but hides that something does exist at f; a caller can't tell it from AbsentAncestor.

options.label: New error class
options.description: A dedicated class (e.g. NotAFolder). Most precise; needs an ERR clause and an ADR, as ResourceLocked did.

questions.question: Sibling clash under coarser equality (write `a` beside existing `A` on a case-insensitive backend): which error?

options.label: AlreadyExists (Recommended)
options.description: Something occupies the slot from the backend's view. path is the caller's key `a`; the message names the existing `A`. Callers already handle this class.

options.label: InvalidPath
options.description: The key is unusable on this store, like a tier rule failure. But it is not a lexical failure, and the same key works on another backend.

options.label: Defer to BE-032
options.description: Collision detection is a backend-encoding matter; leave the error choice to whoever specifies BE-032.

questions.question: Open item 4: a child store at key string c where no folder has Key c. What is the child?

options.label: Lazy: empty until written (Recommended)
options.description: If c is Absent or AbsentAncestor, the child is the one-entity store (only its root); its first write creates c and its missing ancestors in the parent. If c is BlockedByItem or Found(item), creating the child is InvalidPath. Matches today's behavior: child() needs no existence check.

options.label: Must exist
options.description: Creating the child requires Found(e, folder); otherwise NotFound or InvalidPath. Simplest model (the child is always a real subtree), but child() then needs a lookup, and multi-tenant setups must create folders first.

options.label: Unchecked
options.description: The child is defined by c alone; any inconsistency (c is an item) surfaces as errors on the child's operations. No rule at creation, but the child's root may not be a folder, breaking TREE-002 for the child's view.

questions.question: Open item 5: a backend that rewrites names on storage (HFS+ → NFD) breaks write-then-list. How does the model keep the round trip?

options.label: Accept only its normal form (Recommended)
options.description: L_b holds only names the backend stores unchanged: norm_b(n) = n. On HFS+ an NFC `é` is rejected (InvalidPath), NFD is accepted. Becomes a per-string rule in §3a; the round trip always holds; the library still never rewrites.

options.label: Backend must give back the written spelling
options.description: The backend's encoding (BE-032) has to return exactly what was written, e.g. by keeping a mapping. Callers see no difference, but such backends need extra state and listings of pre-existing data can't be fixed.

options.label: Defer to BE-032
options.description: Keep the open note; whoever specifies BE-032 decides.

questions.question: Open item 6a: what is Σ, the alphabet names are written in?

options.label: Unicode scalar values (Recommended)
options.description: Every code point except surrogates. Every name is then encodable as UTF-8, which every backend can carry. Names on a POSIX disk or SFTP server that aren't valid UTF-8 are unreachable, a cost like `\`.

options.label: Bytes
options.description: Σ = the 256 byte values; a key string is a byte string. Reaches every POSIX name, but a caller's text needs an encoding before it is a key, and S3/Azure (UTF-8 only) narrow L_b to valid UTF-8 anyway.

options.label: All code points, surrogates too
options.description: Matches what a Python str can hold (incl. surrogate escapes for undecodable bytes). Reaches non-UTF-8 POSIX names; L_b of UTF-8 backends must then reject lone surrogates.

questions.question: Open item 6b: in what unit are length limits stated?

options.label: Each backend's own unit (Recommended)
options.description: L_b states its limits as the backend measures them: S3 key 1024 UTF-8 bytes, Windows name 255 UTF-16 units, etc. Exact per backend; L_shared takes the strictest of each after converting.

options.label: One library unit
options.description: All limits restated in one unit (e.g. UTF-8 bytes). Simpler to compare, but a conversion is approximate for some backends and must be conservative, rejecting some keys a backend would accept.

questions.question: Open item 7: which language does a store accept, the backend's own (L_floor ∩ L_b) or the portable one (L_floor ∩ L_shared)?

options.label: Backend's own; portable opt-in (Recommended)
options.description: Default L_b: every object the backend can hold (e.g. `a:b` on S3) stays reachable. A store can opt into L_shared to guarantee its keys work on every backend. Declared and observable, like Sep_S.

options.label: Portable by default; opt-out
options.description: Default L_shared: keys move between backends without surprises. Existing data with names outside L_shared (`:` on S3, `CON` on Linux) is unreachable unless the store opts out.

options.label: Always the backend's own
options.description: No portable mode: L_shared is documentation only. Simplest; portability is the caller's job.

questions.question: Which method for the spike?

options.label: Hypothesis first, formal later (Recommended)
options.description: Executable model + property tests now (fast, counterexamples shrink to minimal inputs). Claims that survive go to Lean afterwards, next to StoreAxioms.lean's Key, for a proof over all inputs.

options.label: Lean directly
options.description: Prove the claims over all inputs, reusing StoreAxioms.lean's Key and chain. Strongest result, but slow to iterate and a wrong claim surfaces as a stuck proof, not a counterexample.

options.label: Alloy
options.description: Bounded counterexample search over small stores, reusing StoreAxioms.als. Good for resolution and child-store claims; weak for strings (ν, ≈, join) since Alloy has no native string model.

options.label: Dafny
options.description: Extend StoreTree.dfy / RootPath.dfy with ν and resolution, verify with the existing Docker script. Proofs plus executable code, at a slower pace than Hypothesis.

questions.question: Where does the spike live?

options.label: Sandbox, standalone (Recommended)
options.description: ../sandbox/key-concept/spike/: own model, no repo imports, run with the repo's hatch env. Throwaway; nothing touches the repo until the research doc.

options.label: Repo spike branch
options.description: Feature branch under tests/ or sdd/research/, reusing tests/test_store_tree.py's reference model. Easier to keep, but repo rules (trace, backlog item) start applying.

questions.question: How should the `\` opt-out be fixed?

options.label: Reject `\` anywhere in the input (Recommended)
options.description: After opt-out, any `\` in the raw input is rejected before the walk: it is a separator the store refuses, not a name character. Restores 'opt-out only rejects more'; `\` leaves L_floor and becomes a rule on R.

options.label: Drop the claim
options.description: Keep the end-position check; the concept states that opt-out can change the meaning of an accepted input (`a\a/..` → ε vs `a`). Simpler rule, weaker guarantee.

questions.question: NUL inside a name that `..` removes (`x\0/..` is accepted as ε). Reject NUL anywhere in the input?

options.label: Yes, anywhere (Recommended)
options.description: NUL is rejected in the raw input before the walk, as spec 004 does; it never denotes anything. Same treatment as `\` after opt-out.

options.label: No, end position only
options.description: Keep NUL in L_floor; a NUL in a popped name is harmless because it never reaches the backend.

questions.question: Finding 5: the research's resolution has four outcomes (Absent vs AbsentAncestor carries depth); accepted BE-032 A.1 has Item/Folder/Nothing with no depth. How does the research doc answer it?

options.label: Align with BE-032 (Recommended)
options.description: §3.7 restates BE-032's three outcomes as the authority (Nothing carrying 'path through an item'); Absent/AbsentAncestor merge into Nothing, with j kept only as how the answer is derived. questions.question: What is child(c) when c reduces to ε (`child("")`, `child(".")`, `child("x/..")`)?

options.label: The store itself (Recommended)
options.description: child(ε) = S: composition is the identity (ε ⊕ k = k), and chaining holds for every d the child accepts, including d → ε (child(c).child(".") = child(c)). CHILD-001 (rejects an empty subpath) stays a real delta in § 9.4/§ 10.

options.label: Refused, InvalidPath
options.description: child() refuses ε like CHILD-001 does, as the operation's own root predicate (§ 3.7). CHILD-001 leaves the deltas; chaining needs ν_c(d) ∉ {Reject, ε}.
